ca_isosceles_peak.blurb: Isosceles Peak is a High Sierra summit on the ridge that separates Palisade Basin from Dusy Basin, reached on foot over Bishop Pass. It has nine alpine routes: four are easy fifth-class or scrambling lines, and the rest run from about 5.6 up to a single 5.10. The granodiorite west face has the best climbing, and most parties stop on the lower west summit even though the east summit is the true high point. A large rockfall changed the west face in recent years, so look closely at what you are climbing. The peak is a backcountry objective, usually done as a camp-based outing from the lakes below.

ca_meadow_roof_boulder.blurb: Meadow Roof Boulder is a prominent boulder with an obvious roof near Way Lake, above Mammoth Lakes, at roughly 9,800 feet. It has nine problems, most of them between V6 and V8, with a few harder ones above that, so it is a stop for strong boulderers rather than newcomers. The roof line is the one people come for, though the other problems on the boulder are worth the time too. The surrounding Lower Meadow zone has patches of shade from lodgepole pines, and landings there are mostly flat enough that one or two pads handle them.

ca_inyo_mono_line_tower.blurb: Inyo Mono Line Tower is a sport crag in the Sub Gorge stretch of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop. It has nine bolted routes: one at 5.8, six in the 5.10 range, and a pair of harder lines at 5.11 and 5.12. The wall stays shaded, and its base sits a little above the water, so moving along it is simpler than at some neighbouring walls. The Sub Gorge as a whole sees few visitors. The steeper Splashdown wall is only about a minute downstream, which makes it easy to combine the two.
